ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: on the left side of the figure is a benzene ring, and the benzene ring has two adjacent substituents: one phenolic hydroxyl group O-H, and the other is an acetyl group C(=O)CH3. On the right side is an anhydride-like structure, with the skeleton R-CH2-C(=O)-O-C(=O)-CH2-R; there are also curved arrows and arrows on oxygen in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring these arrows. Reasoning: the left-side o-hydroxyacetophenone fragment can be written as CC(=O)c1ccccc1O. For the right-side anhydride-like fragment, the two R substitution positions are represented with the wildcard *, giving *CC(=O)OC(=O)C*. The two fragments are separate structures in the figure, so they are connected with a dot, giving *CC(=O)OC(=O)C*.CC(=O)c1ccccc1O.

Convert the left fragment to SMILES as CC(=O)c1ccccc1O. Convert the right fragment by replacing each R substituent with a wildcard attachment atom, giving *CC(=O)OC(=O)C*.
